subject: Taxes
title: Why People Cheat on Taxes
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why People Cheat on Taxes usable.

hook.text: The US 'tax gap'—the difference between what's owed and what's paid—is $688 billion annually.

buildup.text: Cash businesses underreport income. Freelancers overstate deductions. Small inflations add up to hundreds of billions.

discovery.text: Why People Cheat on Taxes reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: But experiments show people cheat less than the model predicts.

climax.text: Tax compliance is a moral decision wrapped in an economic one. People weigh conscience as much as consequences.

punchline.text: $688 billion gap, mostly small fudges. Conscience, not audits, restrains it.

quiz.question: What is the US annual 'tax gap'?
